decision.interpretation: The exact BAD-FIBER name or f=h(G) complexity theorem was not found. Nevertheless, the classification is an immediate linear-size corollary of standard Circuit-SAT and is not defensible as a substantive theorem contribution. Search absence is not evidence that the exact wording is historically new.

proof_receipt.membership: BAD-FIBER is in NP: guess two assignments u and v, evaluate G(u), G(v), f(u), and f(v), then verify G(u)=G(v) and f(u) differs from f(v). Circuit evaluation and comparison are polynomial time.
proof_receipt.hardness_source: Boolean Circuit-SAT, stated NP-complete by Böhler et al. at local-text:73-80 and Proposition 3.1 at local-text:421-422.
proof_receipt.reduction: Given a Boolean circuit C(x), construct one additional input b, let the observation circuit G(x,b) be the constant 0 circuit, and let f_C(x,b)=b AND C(x). The construction adds constant size beyond C.
proof_receipt.forward: If C has a satisfying assignment x*, then u=(x*,1) and v=(x*,0) have equal observation G=0 and outputs f_C(u)=1, f_C(v)=0, so they form a bad fiber.
proof_receipt.reverse: If a bad fiber exists, the two f_C values differ. One value is therefore 1, which requires b=1 and C(x)=1. Hence C is satisfiable.
proof_receipt.conclusion: Circuit-SAT many-one reduces to BAD-FIBER in linear size, so BAD-FIBER is NP-hard and therefore NP-complete. Exact CIRCUIT-IDENTIFIABLE is its complement by the constant-on-fibers criterion, so it is coNP-complete.
proof_receipt.equivalence_cross_check: Jordan Proposition 1, local-text:24-34, states Boolean-circuit equivalence is coNP-complete and identifies a differing input as the concise complement witness.

what_remains: The terminology and synthesis of observation factorization may still be expository contributions, but T-01, the two-copy SAT encoding, and the T-11 complexity classification are not defensible as new mathematical results.
No claim is made that the bounded search proved historical absence of the exact BAD-FIBER name.
No additional citation expansion is justified for evaluating T-11.
